title: The 60-Second Side Hustle: PART THREE - my honest review (9/10)
description:
I just finished it. Here's who it's for — and how I'd rate it.

Part 3, the verdict. Quick recap: my first brand deal on JoinBrands was reviewing a book about landing brand deals, written by JoinBrands' own co-founders, Leo Limin and Ian Sells. Paid deal or not, here's my honest take.

PART 3 — THE VERDICT
What it covers: what to sell and at what price points, finding your niche, writing hooks, and using the data TikTok already gives you.

Best part for beginners: the chapter on knowing your worth. Set a starting rate, then raise it once you've got the numbers to back it up.

The part that hit home: staying compliant so your videos don't get flagged. I've had videos flagged without understanding why, and the book walks you through appealing when you didn't break a rule.

Why not a 10: I wanted more depth. It's short and to the point — about three hours — and at 1.5x you'll fly through it. Other than that, it's a solid 9/10.

Who it's for: anyone curious about making videos that sell, even with a 9-to-5.

▶ Part 1 — the listen: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aCOSYOTjrgs
▶ Part 2 — the Hook Trifecta: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=638wLmZOsOI

title: The 60 Second Side-Hustle: PART 2 · THE HOOK TRIFECTA (and my favorite chapter of this audiobook)
description:
Part 2 · Title: The Hook Trifecta — my favorite chapter of The 60-Second Side Hustle audiobook

Three hooks. First three seconds. Did this one work on you?

Part 2 of my series on The 60-Second Side Hustle — the book I reviewed for my first brand deal on JoinBrands, written by the company's co-founders, Leo Limin and Ian Sells.

PART 2 — THE ONE CHAPTER I PUT TO WORK
The best chapter in the book is about the first three seconds of a video. They call it the Hook Trifecta:
1. What they see
2. What they read on the screen
3. The first thing you say
Each one says something different, and the point is to keep people watching to the end.

So I tried it on Part 1. What you see: the book cover and me pressing play. What you read: "No time to read? Same." What you hear: "Knocked it out in a few walks and drives around town." All three, inside three seconds — and this video breaks it down frame by frame.

That one chapter changed how I start every video.

▶ Part 1 — the listen: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aCOSYOTjrgs
